seoTitle: How to Use Gumroad to Build an Email List
metaDescription: Grow your email list on Gumroad by creating a free lead magnet product, setting up an automated Workflow for new subscribers, and writing a welcome email.
intro: Gumroad isn't just a checkout page — it has its own subscriber tools built in, so you can capture emails and follow up with people automatically without bolting on a separate email service. The two pieces that make this work are a free product that gives people a reason to hand over their email, and a Workflow that fires the moment someone subscribes. This guide walks through both, using what's actually on screen in Gumroad's dashboard and Workflow builder, so you can set up the same automated welcome sequence for your own audience.

steps.heading: Understand what Gumroad's platform is built for
steps.body: Gumroad's public homepage leads with a running total of what creators earned in the last week, alongside quotes from people selling brush packs, templates, and content tutorials. It's a reminder that Gumroad is built around individual creators selling directly to an audience, which is exactly why the platform bakes in subscriber and follower tools rather than treating email capture as an afterthought. If you're building a list here, you're doing it on a platform whose whole model depends on you having repeat customers to sell to.

image.caption: Gumroad's homepage, which leads with creator earnings and testimonials rather than a generic product pitch — a hint that the platform is built around ongoing audience relationships.

steps.heading: Get oriented in your dashboard
steps.body: Once you're logged in, the dashboard's left-hand menu is where everything lives: Products, Emails, Workflows, Sales, and Affiliates all sit in their own sections. The "Getting started" checklist at the top is worth reading closely — one of its cards is literally labeled "Build your tribe: Get your first follower," which tells you Gumroad treats follower growth as a core milestone, not a side feature. The Activity panel below tracks balance and earnings, but for list-building purposes, the two menu items you'll actually use are Emails and Workflows.

image.caption: The Gumroad dashboard after signup, with the "Getting started" checklist calling out following and first-sale milestones, and Emails and Workflows both available in the left menu.

steps.heading: Create a free product as your lead magnet
steps.body: Before any of the automation matters, you need a reason for someone to give you their email. Go to Products and create a new one priced at $0 — a short guide, a template, or a small tool related to what you eventually plan to sell. Keep the description honest about what's inside; a lead magnet that overpromises just produces subscribers who unsubscribe the moment they see your next email. Once it's published, anyone who claims it becomes both a customer on your Sales list and a subscriber you can message going forward.

steps.heading: Build a Workflow triggered by new subscribers
steps.body: This is where Gumroad's automation actually happens. Under Workflows, start a new one and give it a name — Gumroad defaults to something generic like "Workflow 2," so rename it to something you'll recognize later. The Trigger section is the key decision: options include Purchase, New subscriber, Member cancels, and New affiliate. Choosing "New subscriber" means the workflow fires the moment someone joins your list, whether they came through your free lead magnet or followed you directly. You can further narrow it with "Has bought," "Has not yet bought," or a subscribed-date range if you only want it to apply to a specific segment.

image.caption: The New Workflow screen, with trigger options for Purchase, New subscriber, Member cancels, and New affiliate, plus optional filters for who the workflow should apply to.

steps.heading: Write the welcome email inside the Workflow
steps.body: Switch to the Emails tab inside your new workflow and you'll find a single email queued up, timed to send some number of hours after the trigger fires — set it to 0 if you want it to go out immediately. Give it a subject line, then write the body in the built-in editor, which supports basic formatting, links, images, and file attachments. The Preview panel on the right shows exactly what the subscriber will receive, footer and all, so you can catch anything that reads oddly before it goes live. Click "Add email" if you want to queue a second message later in the sequence instead of sending just one.

image.caption: The Workflow's Emails tab, with a welcome message being drafted and a live preview on the right showing exactly what the new subscriber will see in their inbox.

steps.heading: Publish the workflow and keep growing the list
steps.body: Nothing sends until you hit Publish in the top right, so double-check the trigger, filters, and email content one more time before you flip it on. After that, every new subscriber gets your welcome message automatically, with zero manual work on your end. From here, growth is mostly about visibility — link your free product from social bios, mention it at the end of paid product descriptions, and check the Sales and Emails sections periodically to see who's engaging, since a list that never gets emailed again is barely different from no list at all.

faq.question: Do I need a paid product to collect emails on Gumroad?
faq.answer: No. A free product works as a lead magnet — anyone who claims it becomes a subscriber you can message through a Workflow, the same as a paying customer.

faq.question: How does Gumroad send emails automatically to new subscribers?
faq.answer: Through the Workflows feature. Create a workflow with a "New subscriber" trigger, write the email in its Emails tab, and publish it — Gumroad handles sending from there.

faq.question: Can I send more than one email in a sequence?
faq.answer: Yes. Inside a workflow's Emails tab you can click "Add email" to queue additional messages, each with its own delay after the trigger.

faq.question: What makes a good lead magnet for Gumroad?
faq.answer: Something quick and genuinely useful related to your paid products — a short guide, checklist, or template — tends to convert well without overpromising.

faq.question: Does growing an email list on Gumroad actually increase sales?
faq.answer: It gives you a direct, repeatable channel to your audience instead of relying on cold traffic, which is why Gumroad surfaces "get your first follower" as an onboarding milestone.
